sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and shows the Elberon station district of Long Branch, where the New York and Long Branch Railroad runs north and south down the middle of the sheet. A trolley right of way lies alongside the railroad on its west side, and the Elberon Station building stands on the east side near Lincoln Avenue. North Lincoln Avenue crosses the sheet from the left edge to the tracks and continues east as Lincoln Avenue, with Albert Place parallel to it near the top. South Lincoln Avenue runs in from the lower left and Norwood Avenue cuts diagonally across the lower left corner. West of the tracks the blocks (101 to 105) are long residential lots with a scatter of frame dwellings, stables and a few larger houses, and a row of small outbuildings stands along the north side of the Lincoln Avenue lots. East of the tracks, along Lincoln Court at the upper right, is a small commercial cluster: Finn Villa (a boarding house), hay and grain, bowling alleys, a garage and repair shop, a fire department with hose wagon and a row of iron clad stores. Southeast of the station the large triangular and curved blocks (106 and 107) are mostly blank, with water pipe lines drawn across them. A fire alarm box stands at the junction of North Lincoln Avenue and the tracks. The bottom edge is marked City Limits and Borough of Deal. A bridge symbol is drawn over the line south of the station.
notes: The sheet is turned about 14 degrees from north (north is up and to the left).
The modern Truax Street appears to follow the drawn trolley right of way beside the railroad.
South Lincoln Avenue and Norwood Avenue have been realigned since 1907; their modern junctions lie 4 to 7 m from the drawn ones, so the placement uses parcel block corners instead.
Elberon Station is lettered on the building east of the tracks.

Printed sheet 6, 60 ft, rot -14. Elberon station (N.Y.&L.B.R.R. and trolley right of way), Albert Pl, N./S. Lincoln Av, Lincoln Ct, Norwood Av. One part; 6 parcel block corners hand-picked (detected junctions 5-10 m off: S Lincoln and Norwood realigned).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 is drawn at 120 feet to an inch and shows the Elberon section of Long Branch between Park Avenue along the top and Lawrence Avenue along the bottom, with the Atlantic Ocean along the right edge. Elberon Avenue, Eaton Avenue and Ocean Avenue run down the sheet, and Lincoln Avenue crosses it about two thirds of the way down. Elberon Square is a short cross street with a small street of the same name running south from it between Eaton and Ocean Avenues. The blocks are large estate lots (numbered 99, 100, 101 and 107) each holding a villa with stables and outbuildings. The largest property is The Elberon Hotel on the oceanfront block east of Ocean Avenue, with a pavilion and bath houses at the shore. Elberon Memorial Presbyterian Church, with its chapel and horse shed, stands on Park Avenue, and an Episcopal Church with a livery and boarding stable lies near Ocean Avenue in the southern part. A fire alarm box and several water pipe lines are marked at the corners. The southern strip is Borough of Deal territory, cut by a City Limits line, and is drawn as a row of narrow numbered lots along Lawrence Avenue. A compass rose sits at the upper left and a Sheet 6 key number at the left edge.
notes: Printed scale is 120 feet to an inch (fitted 3.34 px/ft); the lead's scale list did not include this sheet.
The sheet is turned about 13 degrees from north.
Modern Stuyvesant Place runs through lots that are not drawn as a street here and was left out.
Printed sheet 7, 120 ft, rot -13. Elberon, Park Av to Lawrence Av, Elberon, Eaton, Ocean Av, Elberon Sq, Lincoln Av. One part.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 is drawn at 120 feet to an inch and continues the Elberon district northward from sheet 7. Park Avenue forms the bottom edge, South Lake Drive runs along the top beside Takanassee Lake, and the Atlantic Ocean lies along the right edge. Elberon Avenue and Ocean Avenue run the length of the sheet, with Lakeside Avenue slanting down the left side. Sycamore Avenue and the shorter Adams street cross the blocks. The lots are large estates (blocks 94 to 98) holding villas, stables, hen houses and greenhouses. Dan Guggenheim's property, with greenhouses and a large house, fills the block between Sycamore and Park Avenues, and another estate in the left half has greenhouses, a windmill and water tank beside a small pond. Water pipe lines are drawn in Ocean and Park Avenues. Takanassee Lake is a shaded strip across the top, and the shoreline appears along the right margin. A compass rose with the north arrow pointing up stands in the upper middle. Fire hydrants and a fire alarm box are marked along Ocean Avenue, and Sheet 7 is keyed at the bottom and Sheet 12 at the top.
notes: Printed scale is 120 feet to an inch (fitted 3.33 px/ft); the lead's scale list did not include this sheet.
Modern Lakeside Avenue is displaced from the drawn Lakeside Avenue and was left out of the control.
Adams is printed without a suffix; today's street is Adams Street.
The sheet is turned about 14 degrees from north.
Printed sheet 8, 120 ft, rot -14. Elberon north, S. Lake Drive to Park Av, Takanassee Lake. One part; Lakeside Av left out (realigned).

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 is drawn at 120 feet to an inch and shows the West End district of Long Branch, turned so that north points to the left. A compass rose in the upper left shows this. Hollywood Avenue runs diagonally from the top centre to the lower left, where it becomes Brookdale Avenue and a straight Hollywood Avenue continues down the left side. Brighton Avenue and the short Mulhearn Street lie to the northwest of it. To the east, Woodgate Avenue and Lenox Avenue enclose a curved block, and Hoey Avenue runs across the upper right to Cedar Avenue, which slants down the right edge. Westwood Avenue crosses the lower part in a long curve, with Monmouth Place and Norwood Avenue parallel below it, and Van Court Avenue enters from the right. The blocks (numbered 66 to 74) are residential, with long narrow lots on the diagonal streets and a few larger houses. William Eisele, florist, has a group of greenhouses near Cedar Avenue. Bowyer Avenue is lettered where it enters at the right edge. The sheet has Sheet 13 keyed at the upper right, Sheet 10 on the right, Sheet 5 at the bottom, and Sheet 25 at the upper left. Water pipe lines are drawn in several of the streets.
notes: Printed scale is 120 feet to an inch (fitted 3.37 px/ft).
North points to the left (rotation about -85 degrees).
Modern Cedar Avenue at Norwood Avenue lies about 6 m from the drawn junction and was left out; the Cedar Avenue and Hoey Avenue junction at the right edge was also left out.
The modern Westwood Avenue turns south to Monmouth Place; that stretch is not drawn.
Printed sheet 9, 120 ft, north to the left (-85). West End: Hollywood, Brookdale, Woodgate, Lenox, Hoey, Cedar, Westwood, Monmouth Pl, Norwood. One part.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 is drawn at 120 feet to an inch with north to the left, and covers the Hollywood area of West End, Long Branch. Hoey Avenue runs across the top and again at the upper right, with Cottage Avenue, Lake Avenue and Overlook Avenue running down from it. The Hollywood Hotel, a large frame building with its cottages (numbered 7 to 19), fills the upper left block between Hoey and Bowyer Avenues. Hollywood Lake, a long narrow artificial lake with a wooden bridge carrying Woodgate Avenue across it, stands near the centre top. Woodgate Avenue crosses the sheet at the middle, and Van Court Avenue runs diagonally below it from the left edge to the right. Kirby Avenue, with a short row of lots and a greenhouse, runs down to Norwood Avenue, which crosses the foot of the sheet beside a long pond with an island. Cedar Avenue lies along the left edge and Highland Avenue along the right edge. Most of the large blocks (numbered 75 to 87) are blank or hold only lot lines, with houses grouped in the lower left and a few buildings at the far right. A compass rose with the north arrow pointing left is in the middle, and keys for Sheets 9, 11 and 5 appear in the margins.
notes: Printed scale is 120 feet to an inch (fitted 3.34 px/ft).
North points to the left (rotation about -96 degrees).
Modern Shrewsbury Avenue, which runs through the Hollywood Hotel grounds, is not drawn as a street and was left out.
Modern Overlook Avenue extends to Van Court Avenue; the drawn street ends well short of it.
Printed sheet 10, 120 ft, north to the left (-96). Hollywood Hotel and lake, Hoey, Cottage, Lake, Overlook, Woodgate, Van Court, Kirby, Norwood. One part.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north to the left, and shows the West End of Long Branch near Takanassee Lake. Green Avenue crosses the upper middle and ends at North Lake Drive, which runs down the right side beside Takanassee Lake. Cottage Avenue enters from the bottom edge at Hoey Avenue and runs up to the railroad. A diagonal band of railroad tracks and a trolley trestle crosses the lower part from the upper left to the right edge, where it reaches the Tintern Manor Water Company's West End pumping station, drawn in pink with its filter house. A second lake or reservoir lies in the lower right corner. Block 92 above Green Avenue and block 91 below it are lines of long lots with single frame dwellings and a few stables. Block 90 near the bottom and the lots at the lower left hold larger houses, numbered cottages 1 to 3 on one side and 8 to 10 on the other. A fire alarm box is marked on Green Avenue, and a compass rose with the north arrow pointing left stands near the lake. Keys for Sheets 12, 14, 13, 10 and 8 are at the margins.
notes: Printed scale is 60 feet to an inch (fitted 6.55 px/ft, 1.6 percent below the atlas constant).
North points to the left (rotation about -90 degrees).
Green Avenue is Greens Avenue today.
The railroad is lettered as the N.Y. & L.B. R.R.; the C.R.R. of N.J. line through North Long Branch is gone.
Only two street junctions were available: a helmert fit, low confidence.
Printed sheet 11, 60 ft, north to the left (-90). Green Av, N. Lake Drive, Cottage Av, Hoey Av, railroad, pumping station. One part; 2-point helmert.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north to the left, and shows the oceanfront at West End, Long Branch. The Atlantic Ocean forms the top edge of the sheet, with a bulkhead or beach shown as a shaded strip. Ocean Avenue crosses the sheet from the left edge to North Lake Drive, which runs down the right side beside Takanassee Lake. Sternberger Avenue enters from the lower left. North of Ocean Avenue the oceanfront block (61) is cut into very large lots, each with a villa, a bathing pavilion or stable near the shore, and a small outbuilding near the beach. South of Ocean Avenue, block 92 holds numbered lots with detached frame dwellings, a stable and, near North Lake Drive, St. Michael's R.C. Church, drawn in pink with brick walls, hot air heat and gas lights. The southern lots are mostly blank. A compass rose and north arrow are at the upper right. Keys for Sheets 8, 11, 14 and 16 appear in the margins.
notes: Printed scale is 60 feet to an inch (fitted 6.65 px/ft).
North points to the left (rotation about -92 degrees).
Only two street junctions were available: a helmert fit, low confidence.
Printed sheet 12, 60 ft, north to the left (-92). Ocean front, Ocean Av, N. Lake Drive, Sternberger Av. One part; 2-point helmert.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north to the top and covers the open ground west of the railroad between Hollywood Avenue at the top and Cedar Avenue at the bottom, on the West End side of Long Branch. Most of the sheet is taken up by the grounds of the Monmouth County Horse Show Association: an oval track drawn in dashed lines, a long curved grand stand, stables and sheds along Hollywood Avenue, and an electric light plant. Hoey Avenue runs down the left side of the sheet, with Lenox Avenue curving in from the west to meet it. Below the show grounds a row of large lots between Hoey Avenue and the railroad carries a few frame dwellings and stables, and more dwellings stand on the south side of Cedar Avenue at the foot of the sheet. Along the right edge the double tracks of the New York and Long Branch Railroad run north to south beside a separate trolley right of way, which crosses Cedar Avenue at a fire alarm box; West End Court is lettered at the top right beyond the tracks, by large buildings with their own outbuildings. Water pipes of 8, 12 and 16 inches meet at the Cedar Avenue crossing, and a 4 inch pipe runs along Hoey Avenue at Cedar Avenue. Large parts of the sheet are empty, unbuilt land.
notes: The Monmouth County Horse Show grounds have since been built over; modern Lenox Avenue east of Hoey Avenue runs across the former track and was left out of the control.
Hollywood Avenue no longer crosses the railroad.
Placed from three detected junctions (one a rail crossing) and the hand-picked Hoey Avenue / Lenox Avenue junction; medium to low confidence.

Printed sheet 13, 60 ft, north up. Monmouth County Horse Show grounds between Hollywood Av and Cedar Av, Hoey Av on the left, Lenox Av from the west, N.Y. & L.B. R.R. and trolley right of way on the right. One part; 3 detected points + hand-picked Hoey/Lenox.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north roughly up, and covers part of the West End of Long Branch just west of the ocean-front blocks shown on sheets 15 and 16. The diagonal of the sheet is Cedar Avenue, which runs from lower left to upper right and ends at 2nd Avenue on the right side; Green Avenue branches south from Cedar Avenue in the lower middle and a short unnamed lane crosses the lower blocks. Sternberger Avenue runs across the lower right corner, and New Court Street opens east from 2nd Avenue near the right edge. Along the left edge the New York and Long Branch Railroad runs down the sheet as a bundle of tracks, with a trolley line curving away from it through the open ground at upper left and crossing Cedar Avenue at a fire alarm box. At the top the sheet shows the lower ends of Hollywood Avenue, West End Court and Palmer Avenue, which continue on sheet 20 and sheet 13. The area is thinly built: large detached dwellings of two and a half stories with stables and outbuildings stand on deep, narrow lots between Cedar Avenue and the ocean-front, and several long blocks in the upper centre are still divided only by lot lines. Block numbers 65, 91 and 92 are printed, and the neighbouring sheets are numbered 13, 20, 15, 16, 11 and 12 around the border. A compass rose with a north arrow stands at the right edge.
notes: Green Avenue is Greens Avenue today.
The lane that runs south from Cedar Avenue to Sternberger Avenue near the middle of the sheet is unnamed on the sheet; it is Wertheim Place today.
A street at the top of the sheet is lettered 'Not opened'.
The control is almost all along Cedar Avenue, with one point on New Court and one on Sternberger Avenue: the rotation and scale rest on few points.
Printed sheet 14, 60 ft, rot -11. Cedar Av west of 2nd Av, railroad at left. One part.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned so that east, the ocean, lies at the top of the page and north to the left; the Atlantic Ocean runs as a blue band along the top edge. It covers the West End oceanfront of Long Branch between the shore and 2nd Avenue, which runs across the bottom of the sheet. At the top, Ocean Avenue curves along the beach and Brighton runs up the page as a broad road to the shore, with the large frame building of the West End Cottage and Casino Company, its hotel and restaurant, and a casino on the seaward side. At the middle left a hotel on West End Plaza is marked as the Takanassee Hotel, being built from plans, and beside it a cement building to be offices stands on the blue-tinted plan. A second Ocean Avenue crosses the sheet at about the middle, with the former Johnson's Club House and the former Pennsylvania Club House south of it. Below this, West End Avenue, Montgomery Avenue, Brighton Avenue and West End Court run down the page to 2nd Avenue as long platted blocks of narrow numbered lots, mostly unbuilt on the west side; Brighton Avenue and West End Court are lined with stores, offices, a telegraph office, a steam fire engine house with hose wagon and a fire alarm box at 2nd Avenue. West End Court at the right carries a row of tin-clad commercial frame buildings and a paint shop. The scale bar stands at the foot of the sheet, and the sheet numbers 17, 16, 20 and 14 are printed around the edges.
notes: West End Avenue is lettered 'Not opened' in part of its length at the lower left.
West End Plaza matches the modern Ocean Boulevard at West End Avenue and Montgomery Avenue, and the Ocean Avenue across the middle of the sheet matches the modern Ocean Avenue at West End Court.
The Takanassee Hotel is drawn as being built from plans.
Printed sheet 15, 60 ft, north to the left (-98). West End oceanfront, West End Plaza (Ocean Blvd), Brighton, Montgomery, 2nd Av. One part.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned so that east, the ocean, lies at the top of the page and north to the left. The Atlantic Ocean and its beach run along the top edge, with the Hollywood Baths, a long narrow bathing pavilion built out from the shore, at upper left. Below the beach lie two bands of long, narrow oceanfront lots, each holding a large detached frame dwelling of two and a half stories, separated by Ocean Avenue, which crosses the sheet from left to right about halfway down. South of Ocean Avenue, Cedar Avenue runs down the page from Ocean Avenue to 2nd Avenue, with New Court at the left and Sternberger Avenue slanting down the right side; the blocks between them are cut into deep lots, several of them numbered, and carry more houses and a few outbuildings. 2nd Avenue crosses the bottom of the sheet; near it at the lower left stand a livery stable and several small dwellings. Block numbers 61, 64 and 92 are printed. Most of the oceanfront lots north of Ocean Avenue are unbuilt except for the houses set well back from the shore. A compass rose with a north arrow is drawn in the ocean at the top, and the scale bar and library stamp stand at the foot. The neighbouring sheets numbered 15, 14 and 12 are named around the borders.
notes: The bathing pavilion at the top left is lettered 'Hollywood Baths'.
New Court is lettered 'New Ct.' on the sheet.
Printed sheet 16, 60 ft, north to the left (-98). Cedar Av to Ocean Av, Sternberger, New Ct, 2nd Av. One part.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north roughly up and covers the oceanfront at the West End of Long Branch between 2nd Avenue on the left and Ocean Avenue on the right, with the beach and the Atlantic as a blue strip at the right edge. Two streets cross the sheet from left to right, rising slightly to the right: Avery Avenue in the upper part and West End Avenue in the lower part, with a large block between them numbered 45 and the blocks above and below numbered 44 and 15. Most of the area is open ground. The dominant structure is the Howland House, a large U-shaped hotel complex of several wings near the right side, lettered as not occupied and to be removed. A few dwellings and outbuildings stand along Avery Avenue and along West End Avenue, and a dilapidated storage building at the lower left is lettered as such. Mathilda Terrace is lettered in the top left corner where the sheet meets sheet 18,. Along the right edge Ocean Avenue runs north and south beside the Boardwalk, which is drawn as a dashed strip with yellow cross-bars, and a water pipe and fire hydrants are marked along it. A compass rose with a north arrow stands near the upper right. The printed sheet numbers 18, 19, 20 and 15 identify the neighbouring sheets, and the title Long Branch and N.J. Coast Vol. I appear in the top left corner.
notes: The Ocean Avenue drawn along the Boardwalk is about 300 m east of 2nd Avenue, farther out than the modern Ocean Boulevard, and is not matched to a modern street.
West End Avenue is lettered 'Not opened' in part of its length.
Only two street junctions (2nd Avenue with Avery Avenue and with West End Avenue) were measured, both on 2nd Avenue: the part is placed as a two-point helmert.
Printed sheet 17, 60 ft, rot -12. West End oceanfront strip, Avery Av, West End Av, 2nd Av. One part; helmert on 2nd Av; beachfront Ocean Av displaced.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north roughly up and covers a strip of the oceanfront at the West End of Long Branch between 2nd Avenue along the left edge and Ocean Avenue and the Boardwalk at the right, with the beach and the Atlantic as a pale blue band on the right. South Bath Avenue crosses the top of the sheet behind a brick wall ten feet high. Below it a large grounds, block 42, is enclosed by a stone wall and holds a private casino and several detached dwellings, among them the building formerly the Long Branch Club, an octagonal-cupola house with wings, near the right edge. Cottage Place runs across the middle of the sheet from 2nd Avenue to Ocean Avenue, with long lots numbered 1 to 9 on its north side and Stern's Villa and other houses on its south side in block 43. Mathilda Terrace crosses the lower part of the sheet with lots on both sides and the houses of block 44, and Avery Avenue appears at the lower right, where it meets Ocean Avenue. A compass rose with a north arrow stands at the upper left. Along the right edge the Boardwalk is shown as a dashed strip with yellow cross-bars and fire hydrants and water pipes are marked in the streets. At the left edge 2nd Avenue runs vertically with the sheet number 26 beyond it, and Eastbourne Avenue is lettered just past the left edge near the foot. The scale bar is at the lower left.
notes: Mathilda Terrace is Matilda Terrace in the modern street data.
The street lettered 'E. Bourne Av.' is Eastbourne Avenue today; the abbreviation is written out here as printed.
The Ocean Avenue drawn along the Boardwalk lies about 300 m east of 2nd Avenue, farther out than the modern Ocean Boulevard, and was not used as control.
Only three junctions were measured, all on 2nd Avenue, so the part is placed as a helmert.
Printed sheet 18, 60 ft, rot -12. Oceanfront strip, South Bath, Cottage Pl, Mathilda Terrace, 2nd Av. One part; helmert on 2nd Av.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left of the page, which is why the streets run in the opposite sense to the other West End sheets. It covers the area west of 2nd Avenue in Long Branch, from Mathilda Terrace and 2nd Avenue at the top to Indiana Avenue at the foot. Sairs Avenue runs across the middle of the sheet, with Eastbourne Avenue crossing it at the left edge, Avery Avenue at the middle and Hulick at the right. A double-tracked line lettered C.R.R. of N.J. crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left to the right, cutting through the blocks north of Sairs Avenue, and a second line lettered N.Y. & L.B. R.R. with sidings runs across the lower part of the sheet; the large block below it, numbered 53, is open ground. The area is thinly built. A few frame dwellings stand on the long lots north of Sairs Avenue and along Eastbourne Avenue and Hulick, Pierce's Stable stands beside the railroad at the middle top, and a few other buildings and sheds stand south of Sairs Avenue near Avery Avenue. A compass rose with a north arrow pointing left stands at the upper left. The blocks are numbered 46 to 50 and 53, the neighbouring sheets 17, 20, 25 and 26 are named at the edges, and the scale bar is at the lower left.
notes: Mathilda Terrace is Matilda Terrace in the modern street data; Hulick is Hulick Street today.
The C.R.R. of N.J. line across the upper part of the sheet no longer exists as a running line and was not used as control.
Printed sheet 19, 60 ft, north to the left (-101). Sairs, Eastbourne, Avery, Hulick, 2nd, Indiana. One part.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left of the page, with 2nd Avenue running across the top. It shows the commercial centre of the West End of Long Branch around the New York and Long Branch railroad station. 2nd Avenue at the top is lined with the large New York Cab Company carriage house, a union hotel, Hendrickson's Hotel, the St. James Hotel and Fern's Cottage. West End Avenue and Brighton Avenue run down the page from 2nd Avenue to Sairs Avenue, with a public school heated and lighted by electricity, a garage and a machine shop between them. Palmer Avenue crosses the right half, where the Knickerbocker Stable Company, a horseshoer and the Hotel Keller and the Melbourne stand in block 65, and West End Court, with a trolley right of way and a street marked not opened, runs along the right edge. Brighton Avenue carries stores, offices and the Dalton Hotel and Brighton Hotel at Sairs Avenue. Below Sairs Avenue the tracks of the railroad and a water pipe cross the sheet and the passenger station and a second station building stand near the right edge. Further down, J. Guire and Brother, coal, hay and grain, the William A. Molter garage and a coal shed fill block 57, and in the lower left the Slawson Decker Company dairy and the Independent Ice Company stand beside block 19, with open land to the left and a compass rose and scale bar at the foot.
notes: Palmer Avenue as drawn lies about 40 m from the modern Palmer Avenue and was not used as control.
Hulick is Hulick Street today.
A street east of Shepard Avenue is lettered 'Not opened', beside a trolley right of way.
Printed sheet 20, 60 ft, north to the left (-99). West End station district, 2nd Av, West End Av, Brighton, Sairs. One part; Palmer Av displaced.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north roughly up the page and covers the western edge of Long Branch, where Norwood Avenue runs down the left side and a double-track railroad runs down the right-hand side of the sheet. The left half is a patchwork of large lots. In the upper left are small frame dwellings and stables along Campbell Avenue and Overton Place, with an unbuilt block of numbered lots between Overton Place, the street lettered Winter and High. Below that the lots along High (Wall) and the Norwood Avenue frontage hold more dwellings, a hotel (the Norwood Av. Hotel) and the shop of A. Hurley and Co., electrical contractors. The lower left is a large block of open land with a few dwellings, bounded by West End Avenue along the foot of the sheet. East of the railroad Wardell Place runs south along the track, and across it Norwood Avenue and Brighton Avenue serve a district of larger frame houses that includes Primary School No. 4. Winter Street and Autumn Place meet Overton Place and the railroad right-of-way in a small triangle at the compass rose. The street grid on the left is regular, while the streets east of the railroad run at an angle to it. Pipe sizes and distances are lettered along several streets, and the sheet number 21 is repeated in the lower and upper right.
notes: Street lettered "Wardell" is lettered with "Pl." following on the second line; modern name is Wardell Place.

The east side of the sheet (Norwood Avenue east of the railroad, Brighton Avenue, Winter Street) does not follow the modern street lines, so only the Norwood Avenue, Overton Place, High Street, West End Avenue and Wardell Place junctions were used as control.
Only five junctions were available: the fit is weak in the east half of the sheet.
The helper read the street lettered High as "High (Wall)"; whether Wall is also lettered on it was not verified.
Printed sheet 21, 60 ft, rot +9. Norwood Av west of the railroad, Overton Pl, High, West End Av, Winter. One part.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with the sheet turned about ten degrees from north, and shows the business edge of western Long Branch between Broadway along the top and Taber Street along the bottom. Along Broadway the frontage is solidly built with stores, a harness shop, a hotel, an Odd Fellows hall and tin shops, with a livery and exchange stable further along. Norwood Avenue runs the full height of the sheet, with the Fire Department chemical and hose house and a furniture store on its west side. Bath Avenue cuts diagonally across the upper right and Pearl Street curves up the right edge; between them, long narrow lots slope towards the diagonal streets and hold dwellings. West of Norwood Avenue are the blocks bounded by Grove Street, Conover and Morford Avenue, mostly dwellings with a mission house of the A.M.E.Z. church. Gerard Avenue crosses the lower left diagonally through large open lots. Taber Terrace and West Bourne Avenue run off the lower right, past the compass rose. The sheet carries the sheet numbers of its neighbours 43, 46, 27, 23 and 22 and shows water pipe and fire alarm box locations on Broadway and Norwood Avenue.
notes: Taber Street is the modern Tabor Street (spelling differs); Taber Terrace appears to correspond to the modern Vanderbilt Avenue (medium confidence, from overlay).
Printed "Grand Av." and "Branchport Av." lie at the sheet top and were not used as control.
Pearl and Conover are printed without a suffix; the modern streets are Pearl Street and Conover Street.
Printed sheet 22, 60 ft, rot +10. Broadway to Taber, Norwood, Bath, Pearl. One part.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north pointing up and to the left, and shows the district around Westbourne Avenue in western Long Branch, between Bath Avenue along the top and Winter and Campbell Avenue along the bottom. The upper third is a row of deep residential lots on the south side of Bath Avenue, most holding single dwellings. Westbourne Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet, with a short row of dwellings on small lots along its north side and Taber Street and Taber Terrace branching off its western end. In the lower centre a diamond-shaped block of lots between Taber Terrace, Winter and the unnumbered street along the foot is partly built. Chandler Place, Summer and Winter form a regular block of long narrow lots in the lower right, with Springdale Avenue curving round its east side and Autumn Place closing it. A large unbuilt tract lies at the lower left between Norwood Avenue, which runs diagonally to the lower left corner, and Taber Street; a compass rose and the north arrow stand on this open ground. Streets crossing the top edge include Emmons, Morrel and Division. Dwellings are of two to two and a half stories.
notes: Taber is the modern Tabor Street; Taber Terrace corresponds to the modern Vanderbilt Avenue (medium confidence, from overlay).
Winter, Summer and Chandler Place do not follow the modern street lines closely; Winter Street / Vanderbilt Avenue and Springdale Avenue junctions were used as control.
Scale 60 feet to an inch as printed; fitted scale 6.57 px/ft agrees.
Printed sheet 23, 60 ft, rot -34. Westbourne Av district. One part.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch, turned about 33 degrees from north, and covers the neighbourhood around High Street, Bath Avenue and Eastbourne Avenue in western Long Branch. Bath Avenue runs along the top and High runs south-west from the foot of Eastbourne Avenue diagonally through the sheet. In the upper left, deep lots on the south side of Bath Avenue hold a handful of large frame dwellings and outbuildings. The upper right quarter is mostly open ground and large lots with a few dwellings, crossed by the compass rose. Below Waverly Place the sheet is filled with small subdivision lots: Waverly Place and Springdale Avenue form a curved block of narrow lots drawn with frame dwellings, while Summer and Springdale run down the left edge. Eastbourne Avenue runs east from High across the right side, with lots 53 to 57 and large unbuilt blocks south of it. The lower part of the sheet is open land and large parcels. A note in the lower left reads Autumn Place Not Opened. Distances in feet are lettered along High Street and Bath Avenue, and sheet numbers 23, 25, 28 and 29 name the neighbouring sheets.
notes: Only two junctions could be used (Eastbourne Avenue / High Street and Bath Avenue / High Street): the fit is a two-point helmert and low confidence, although its scale (6.66 px/ft) agrees with the 60 ft scale printed on the sheet.
The detector placed High Street / Springdale Avenue about 16 m from where the modern junction projects; that junction was left out of control as unreliable.
Autumn Place is noted as not opened on the sheet.
Printed sheet 24, 60 ft, rot -33. High St, Bath, Eastbourne, Springdale, Summer, Waverly. One part; 2-point helmert (Springdale, Summer, Waverly displaced).

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 is printed at 120 feet to an inch, turned about 30 degrees from north, and covers the western outskirts of Long Branch between Bath Avenue at the top and Brighton Avenue near the foot. Westwood Avenue runs down the left side, Eastbourne Avenue crosses the upper part, and Indiana Avenue runs diagonally from the top centre to the lower right corner past the compass rose. Most of the area is large lots and open land, numbered by block (13, 14, 33, 54, 55, 56, 57) with a handful of detached frame dwellings, outbuildings and the James Ambacher greenhouse range. West End Avenue crosses the lower third, and Mulhern runs south from it towards Brighton Avenue between smaller lots with dwellings and a few sheds. In the lower right, off Indiana Avenue, a large building with a steam laundry (Hollywood Steam Laundry) stands on the corner of a long block. The sheet shows 50-foot and 55-foot street widths lettered along the avenues and a few water pipe and fire alarm box symbols near Brighton Avenue. Sheet numbers 24, 29, 30, 26, 19, 20, 9 and 71 are given at the edges.
notes: This sheet is printed "Scale 120 Ft. to an Inch"; the fitted scale is about 3.34 px/ft, so scale_ft 120 should be set for it in atlas.json.
Mulhern appears to occupy the line of the modern Hoey Street; it was not used as control.
Seven junctions on Westwood, Eastbourne, Bath, West End, Brighton and Indiana Avenues were used.
Printed sheet 25, 120 ft, rot -30. Westwood Av, Eastbourne, Indiana Av outskirts. One part.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points to the left, and shows the district around Sairs Avenue, Cottage Avenue and Eastbourne Avenue, west of the Long Branch business centre. Two railroads cross the sheet: the C.R.R. of N.J. diagonally in the upper third, and the N.Y. & L.B. R.R., with a broad yard of parallel tracks and a watchman's house, along the lower third. Between them Sairs Avenue runs across the middle of the sheet with large lots, mostly with single frame dwellings, on both sides; Bath Avenue (and South Bath Avenue at the upper left) runs down the left side. Darby's Livery stable and several large dwellings stand on the block between 2nd Avenue and the Central Railroad. Cottage Avenue separates the two halves of the upper blocks, and Eastbourne Avenue runs down the right edge. South of the N.Y. & L.B. R.R. a large open lot (34) holds one dwelling, and a small pink building stands near its upper right corner. Indiana Avenue runs along the foot of the sheet. A third avenue is lettered Third Av. at the Bath Avenue end of the tracks. Pipe and fire alarm information is lettered along the streets.
notes: Cottage Avenue is the modern Cottage Place.
North is to the left of the sheet (fitted rotation about -102 degrees).
Six junctions were used, including one rail crossing (Bath Avenue and the N.Y. & L.B. R.R.); leave-one-out is 3.9 m.
Printed sheet 26, 60 ft, north to the left (-102). Sairs Av, Cottage Pl; both railroads. One part.

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch, turned about 33 degrees from north, and shows the western end of Long Branch's Broadway and its junctions with Bath Avenue, Pearl, Morrel and Willow Avenue. Broadway runs diagonally from the lower left to the top, lined by dwellings and a few institutional buildings, among them Primary School No. 1, a blacksmith and a church hall. Morris Avenue crosses the top of the sheet, with the Stiener and Son factory for sleeping garments, Factory No. 8, drawn in detail on its south side. Willow Avenue and Exchange Avenue run south-east between rows of dwellings, and Morrel runs diagonally down through the centre between narrow lots to Bath Avenue. Emmons crosses the lower part to the Baptist church (First Baptist Church) on the block between Emmons and Pearl. Bath Avenue lies along the foot of the sheet, with a regular row of dwellings fronting it. Spring Street joins Morrel at the right edge. Washington Street runs off the lower left corner beside Broadway. Much of the upper left is blank, containing only the compass rose.
notes: Morrel is spelled with one L on the sheet; the modern street is Morrell Street.
Exchange Avenue is not in the current street data (the modern Exchange Place lies along a different line).
Fitted scale 6.70 px/ft; six junctions were used.
Printed sheet 27, 60 ft, rot -34. Broadway, Morrel, Willow. One part.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north pointing to the upper left, and covers a residential district of western Long Branch between Morris Avenue along the top and Bath Avenue along the bottom. Division runs down the middle of the sheet and Prospect along the right edge; Willow Avenue and Exchange Avenue cross both of them, and Spring crosses Division low on the sheet. Morrel runs diagonally across the lower left corner. The blocks are divided into narrow numbered lots, mostly holding frame dwellings of two stories with stables and small outbuildings behind, and many lots, especially on the left and in the lower right, are empty. A large yellow building stands against the left margin at the top. Between Exchange Avenue and Spring, on the right side of Division, lies a Base Ball Park with its grand stand drawn at the upper left corner, and below it is a block of large lots with a few substantial houses. Six inch water pipes are marked along the top and bottom margins, with fire alarm boxes at the upper and lower right corners and hydrants at several street corners. A strip of the neighbouring sheet 29 is drawn along the right edge, showing the ends of Poole Avenue and Cleveland Avenue beyond Prospect.
notes: North points to the upper left of the sheet.
Modern names: Exchange Avenue is Exchange Place, Morrel is Morrell Street, Spring is Spring Street, Division is Division Street and Prospect is Prospect Street.
Placed from ten detected junctions; Division Street / Spring Street and Exchange Place / Willow Avenue were not detected.
Printed sheet 28, 60 ft, rot -34. Morris Av to Bath Av, Division, Prospect, ball park. One part.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north to the upper left, and shows the ground east of Prospect between Morris Avenue at the top and Bath Avenue at the bottom. Morris Avenue and Willow Avenue run from left to right across the upper half and converge toward the right, enclosing wedge shaped blocks; Poole Avenue and Cleveland Avenue cross the middle of the sheet from Prospect at the left edge. At the top left, in a large open lot bounded by Morris and Willow Avenues, stand the Grammar School and the Chattle High School, both drawn in pink as brick buildings with their heating and lighting noted beneath. The lots along Morris Avenue and both sides of Willow Avenue carry small frame dwellings, a hall, a creamery with wagon shed, cold storage and ice house, and an Adams Express Co. building near the upper right. South of Poole Avenue the lots are large and mostly empty, with a few dwellings and a greenhouse on the larger tracts near the bottom of the sheet. Slocum Avenue and Cherry Street enter Morris Avenue from the north, and High Street joins Bath Avenue at the foot. A compass rose stands near the top centre, and six and eight inch water pipes run along the margins.
notes: North points to the upper left of the sheet.
The street along the left edge south of Cleveland Avenue is lettered Exchange Avenue; above Cleveland Avenue the same street is lettered Prospect, and the modern name is Prospect Street.
Slocum Avenue and Cherry Street north of Morris Avenue were not matched to modern streets (modern Cherry Street does not reach Morris Avenue) and were not used.

Placed from five detected junctions along Prospect Street and a hand-picked Bath Avenue / High Street junction; rotation and scale agree with sheet 28, but the right side of the sheet has no control. Low to medium confidence.
Printed sheet 29, 60 ft, rot -33. Morris/Willow wedge blocks, schools, Poole, Cleveland. One part; points mostly on Prospect St.

sheet-30-1.description: Sheet 30, part 1, is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north to the upper left. It covers the strip between Westwood Avenue on the left and the broad right of way of the New York and Long Branch Railroad, which crosses the sheet diagonally from the top to the lower right, with Morris Avenue at the top left corner and Bath Avenue along the bottom. West Avenue, a wide street running beside the tracks, also runs diagonally and meets Bath Avenue and Indiana Avenue at the foot of the sheet. The lots along Westwood Avenue are mostly narrow with two story frame dwellings; Willow Avenue and Cleveland Avenue cross at the left, and a hay and ware house stands near the middle. Between West Avenue and the tracks the ground is open, with a large building and a fire alarm box near the top, a freight depot with its open platform, an ice house and a few small buildings drawn among the many tracks. Third Avenue and Avenue A are lettered at the right edge beyond the tracks. A heavy ruled box in the upper right corner of the sheet, which shows Morris, Westwood and West Avenues in a different position, is cut out of this part. A compass rose stands at the top beside the box, and a fire alarm box and several hydrants are marked.
notes: North points to the upper left of the sheet.
The heavy ruled box at the top right of the sheet is a separate area and is not part of this mask; see the sheet notes.

Placed from five detected junctions along Westwood Avenue and Willow Avenue and two hand-picked junctions (Bath / Indiana / West and Morris / Westwood), without parcel reference because the parcel centres of Westwood Avenue lie 10 m from the street. Medium confidence.
Printed sheet 30, 60 ft, rot -33. Railroad and West Av, Westwood, Willow, Poole, Cleveland. Two parts: 1 main (use_parcels false); 2 heavy-ruled box at top right (Morris, Westwood, West Av) unplaced.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: heavy-ruled box at top right: Morris, Westwood and West Avenues (no usable junction; shows the area of sheet 38 again; needs carried points from sheet 38 (step 6b)).

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left. It covers the ground between Morris Avenue, a long street running from the top left to the foot of the sheet, and Pavilion Avenue, with 2nd Avenue across the top and 3rd Avenue across the bottom. Between Morris Avenue and Pavilion Avenue lie two rows of deep lots; the left row holds frame dwellings of two and a half stories, Carl H. Schultz's Mineral Water Depot with its sheds and beer storage, and Hotel Ten Eyck at the corner of Morris and 3rd Avenue. East of Pavilion Avenue most of the ground is taken by the Monmouth Memorial Hospital, with its main building in pink, nurses' quarters and wards, a steam laundry and a crematory; Avenue B runs along the right edge. The tracks of the C.R.R. of N.J. run along 2nd Avenue at the top. Below 3rd Avenue, at the bottom, are the offices of the New York and Long Branch Railroad, the passenger station, Adams and U.S. Express offices and the main tracks of the New York and Long Branch Railroad. A compass rose stands near the top left, and six and twelve inch water pipes are marked in the streets.
notes: North points to the left of the sheet.
Avenue B has no counterpart in the modern street network and was not used.

Placed from three detected junctions (3rd Avenue with Morris and Pavilion Avenues, and 2nd Avenue with Pavilion Avenue), an exact fit; the 2nd Avenue junction is measured beside the C.R.R. of N.J. tracks. Low confidence.
Printed sheet 31, 60 ft, north to the left (-90). Morris, Pavilion, 2nd and 3rd Av, Monmouth Memorial Hospital. One part; exact fit on 3 points.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the left, and covers a large, nearly empty tract west of Bath Avenue between the two railroads of Long Branch. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the upper part of the sheet diagonally, with the Bath Avenue station where North Bath Avenue and South Bath Avenue fork from Bath Avenue at the top right. The New York and Long Branch Railroad runs along the bottom edge. 3rd Avenue crosses the lower part of the sheet from the left edge to Bath Avenue, and Sairs Avenue leaves Bath Avenue to the right just above it. Two streets are laid out down from the railroad to 3rd Avenue, Avenue B on a slant and Avenue A, which is marked as not opened, but nothing is built along them. The only buildings are a few dwellings beside the Central railroad at the upper left, a group of stables, sheds, a caretaker's house and a green house in the middle of block 29, two large buildings at its right side near Bath Avenue, and a building by the lower railroad at the bottom left. Water pipes of 8 and 12 inches are marked in Bath Avenue, 3rd Avenue and Sairs Avenue, with a hydrant at the corner of 3rd Avenue.
notes: Avenue A and Avenue B have no modern counterpart in OpenStreetMap; the tract has been redeveloped.

Placed from three points along Bath Avenue (3rd Avenue, Sairs Avenue and the New York and Long Branch Railroad crossing) as a helmert; rotation rests on 1700 px of one street. Low confidence away from Bath Avenue.
The 1907 fork of North and South Bath Avenue does not match the modern junctions (about 40 m and 250 m off), so they were left out.

Printed sheet 32, 60 ft, north to the left. Nearly empty tract between the C.R.R. of N.J. (top) and N.Y. & L.B. R.R. (bottom), 3rd Av, Avenue A (not opened), Avenue B, Bath Av, Sairs Av, N. and S. Bath Av. One part; control only along Bath Av (helmert).

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north near the top and covers the Long Branch seafront between 2nd Avenue at the left and Ocean Avenue at the right, with the Board Walk and the beach along the right edge. 1st Avenue runs up the middle of the sheet; Avenue B crosses between 2nd and 1st Avenues, North Bath Avenue runs diagonally from the lower left to Ocean Avenue, and South Bath Avenue crosses the foot of the sheet. East of 1st Avenue the lots run through to Ocean Avenue and hold large seaside frame houses and, in the middle, Pannacis Hotel; at the foot on South Bath Avenue stands The Scarboro, a hotel with laundry, kitchen, pavilion and platform. West of 1st Avenue the blocks are smaller, with dwellings, a synagogue, a boarding house and, at the lower left, the Siegel Cooper Co's Employees Seaside Home. The Central R.R. of N.J. runs down the left edge with the Bath Av. Station near the lower left. A compass rose stands at the top, and six, ten and twelve inch water pipes are marked in the streets.
notes: Modern names: 1st Avenue is Ocean Boulevard, Avenue B is Dunbar Avenue, and North Bath Avenue west of 1st Avenue is Bath Avenue.
Placed from eight detected junctions; one duplicate node at 1st Avenue and North Bath Avenue was rejected.
Printed sheet 33, 60 ft, rot -15. Seafront 2nd Av to Ocean Av, North and South Bath Av; 1st Av = Ocean Blvd. One part.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north to the top and covers the Long Branch ocean front north of sheet 33, between the Board Walk and the Atlantic Ocean at the right and the tracks of the Central R.R. of N.J. at the left. Morris Avenue crosses the top of the sheet diagonally, Pavilion Avenue runs across the lower middle and curves up to meet Ocean Avenue, 1st Avenue runs up and down the middle and Ocean Avenue runs along the right. The large block at the left, between the railroad and 1st Avenue, is mostly open with a few houses at its edge. East of 1st Avenue, between Morris and Pavilion Avenues, the deep lots run through to Ocean Avenue and hold seaside dwellings. Below Pavilion Avenue is the Atlantic Hotel with its dining room and kitchen, then A. Kurrus's ice house and ice cream factory, and rows of dwellings and boarding houses along 1st Avenue down to the foot of the sheet. The shore line, with the Board Walk drawn in yellow bands, forms the right edge, and 2nd Avenue is lettered at the left margin. A compass rose stands at the upper left.
notes: Modern names: 1st Avenue is Ocean Boulevard.
Modern Ocean Avenue at Pavilion Avenue lies about 20 m from the 1907 Ocean Avenue and was left out of the control.
Placed from two detected junctions on 1st Avenue and two hand-picked parcel block corners at 2nd Avenue and Pavilion Avenue; the fitted scale is about 3 percent below the atlas value. Low confidence.
Printed sheet 34, 60 ft, rot -7. Ocean front, Morris, Pavilion, 1st Av, Ocean Av, Atlantic Hotel. One part; Ocean Av displaced about 20 m.

sheet-35.description: Sheet 35 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left, with the Atlantic Ocean, the Board Walk and Ocean Avenue along the top of the sheet. Chelsea Avenue, Franklin Avenue and Morris Avenue run down the sheet from Ocean Avenue to 2nd Avenue at the foot. At the ocean end of the block between Chelsea and Franklin Avenues stand Cranmers Bath Houses: a row of long narrow bath house buildings with an office, water tanks and a bathing pool. Below them dwellings and boarding houses line Chelsea Avenue, and the rest of the block next to Franklin Avenue is open. Between Franklin and Morris Avenues the deep lots carry frame dwellings and a boarding house near Ocean Avenue, with a short street, 1st Avenue, leaving Morris Avenue at the right edge. The Central R.R. of N.J. crosses the lower half of the sheet diagonally, with the Chelsea Av. Station beside Chelsea Avenue, and then runs along 2nd Avenue at the foot. Dwellings and a small chapel stand between the railroad and 2nd Avenue. A compass rose stands at the top right, a fire alarm box at 2nd Avenue, and six, ten and twelve inch water pipes are marked in the streets.
notes: North points to the left of the sheet.
Modern names: 1st Avenue is Ocean Boulevard.

The detected Chelsea Avenue / Ocean Boulevard point falls where Chelsea Avenue crosses the railroad at the Chelsea Av. Station; a fit from the two 2nd Avenue junctions alone agrees with it to within 2 degrees of rotation and 0.3 percent of scale.
Placed from four detected junctions. Medium to low confidence.
Printed sheet 35, 60 ft, north to the left (-83). Chelsea, Franklin, Morris Av, bath houses, C.R.R. One part.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and shows the oceanfront of Long Branch at its eastern edge, between Broadway along the top and Chelsea Avenue along the bottom, with the Atlantic Ocean down the right side. The sheet is nearly square to north. The large block in the centre, bounded by Broadway, Abbotsford Avenue, Laird Street and Ocean Avenue, is mostly open ground and holds the Old Casino near the top and the New Casino, a long building, near its middle. Along the shore Ocean Avenue runs down the right side with the Board Walk beside it, public pavilions and a few small buildings, and a pale blue band marks the water of the ocean and a creek along the beach. South of Laird Street the sheet shows the Mansion House at the corner of Ocean Avenue, the Columbia Baths, a long set of bath houses with an office, a storage building for fishermen's tackle, and a lot marked as the site of a merry-go-round to be built. On the left, between Mill and Abbotsford Avenue, are blocks of hotels, saloons, a bottling works, a wagon house belonging to the city and the Neptune house, with small dwellings facing 1st Avenue and the streets to the south. Along the left edge the railroad tracks run down the page beside a lumber yard and its sheds. A few water pipes and hydrants are marked in the streets. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 52 and 53 above, 42 to the left and 35 below.
notes: The part is placed from a single hand-picked junction (Laird and Ocean Avenue) with the scale and rotation taken from the config, and is low confidence.
1st Avenue appears to be the modern Ocean Boulevard; the modern junction of Garfield Avenue, Laird Street and Ocean Boulevard falls within a few metres of where 1st Avenue meets Laird on the sheet.
Abbotsford Avenue is not a street the detector uses; Laird is today Laird Street.
Printed sheet 36, 60 ft, rot +3. Oceanfront, Laird, Ocean Av, Broadway. One part; anchored on one hand-picked junction.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch, turned on the page so that north points to the left, and covers the residential blocks west of downtown Long Branch between 2nd Avenue along the top and 3rd Avenue along the bottom. Chelsea Avenue runs down the left edge, Franklin Avenue down the middle and Morris Avenue down the right side, so the sheet shows two long blocks each side of Franklin Avenue. The lots are deep and mostly hold single frame dwellings of two and a half stories with stables and outbuildings behind; a few boarding houses stand among them. On Chelsea Avenue near 2nd Avenue is the Star of the Sea Day School and Academy. At the lower right corner, on 3rd Avenue at Morris Avenue, is McIlhinney's Hotel with its parlor and saloon, and at the lower left Westwood Avenue cuts diagonally across the corner of 3rd Avenue. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches are marked in 2nd and 3rd Avenues and in Franklin Avenue, with a fire alarm box at Franklin Avenue and 2nd Avenue and hydrants at several corners. Much of the area between Franklin and Morris Avenues is still open, with the back parts of the lots undeveloped.
notes: North points to the left of the sheet.
Westwood Avenue, Franklin Avenue and 3rd Avenue meet in a cluster of three modern junctions within 50 m; Westwood Avenue was left out of the control.
Printed sheet 37, 60 ft, north to the left (pilot). 2nd Av to 3rd Av between Chelsea Av and Morris Av, Franklin Av; Star of the Sea Academy. One part.

sheet-38.description: Sheet 38 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and is turned so that north points to the left, about 83 degrees from the top of the page, and shows the West End district of Long Branch south of the railroad. 3rd Avenue runs along the top, with Franklin Avenue joining it from above and Westwood branching away from it at the upper left and running diagonally down the sheet beside a row of frame dwellings. The tracks and yards of the New York and Long Branch Railroad cross the upper middle in a wide curved band, with a turntable, an engine house, coal platforms and an ice house along them. At the upper left is the First Presbyterian Church. In the upper right are the Sherman Mill and Elevator, a feed mill, a store house, the Long Branch Beef Company cold storage, a summer home for children and a boarding house on the south side of 3rd Avenue, and at the right edge the Triangle Hotel, a bottling works, a stone yard and the Armour and Company beef storage near the junction of West Avenue and Morris Avenue. The lower two thirds of the sheet are filled by long narrow blocks of dwellings laid out between Jeffrey, Cherry, Hillside, Morris and Slocum, with Chelsea Avenue down the left edge. A good many lots in the lower blocks are small, with detached frame dwellings, and many of the buildings are numbered. Water pipes of 6, 8 and 12 inches are marked in several streets. A compass rose in the lower right shows the turned orientation. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 37 above, 41 and 40 to the left, 39 below and 31, 30 and 29 to the right.
notes: North points to the left of the sheet.
Westwood is today Westwood Avenue, Jeffrey is Jeffrey Street and Cherry is Cherry Street.
The modern Franklin Avenue and Westwood Avenue junction was left out of the control: the sheet draws no Franklin Avenue south of 3rd Avenue.
The part has few junctions and a leave-one-out error of about 8 m, so its position is low confidence.
Printed sheet 38, 60 ft, north to the left (-83). Franklin, Westwood, 3rd Av, Jeffrey, Cherry. One part.

sheet-39.description: Sheet 39 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and is turned so that north points to the upper right, about 53 degrees clockwise from the top of the page. It covers the area of western Long Branch where Broadway, Chelsea Avenue and the railroad meet. Broadway runs along the top of the sheet, with a row of detached frame dwellings on its south side and the pointed blocks between it and Chelsea Avenue held mostly by lumber and coal yards. Morris Avenue runs down the left edge, crossed by Division Street and Prospect Street. Chelsea Avenue and Slocum Avenue run diagonally from the left side towards the lower middle, lined on both sides by narrow lots with dwellings. The largest feature is the yard of the Edwards Lumber and Coal Company in the centre of the sheet, enclosed by long lumber sheds and a coal trestle, with lumber stacked in numbered piles in its interior. A broad band of railroad tracks of the New York and Long Branch line runs down the right of the sheet, crossing Broadway and bordering the yard, with a hardware, paints and oils store, an office and T. L. Slocum and Company's coal yard with its wood shed on the east side of the tracks. 7th Avenue is lettered at the right of the lumber yard. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches, fire alarm boxes and hydrants are marked in the streets. A compass rose stands at the right edge. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 47 and 48 above, 40 to the right, 38 below and 27, 28 and 29 to the left.
notes: North points to the upper right of the sheet.
The sheet has few usable junctions; the part is controlled mainly by points along Morris Avenue and Broadway, with one railroad crossing, and is low confidence.
Division Street, Prospect Street and Dudley Street junctions were placed by hand because only one cross street of each was drawn in full.
Printed sheet 39, 60 ft, rot +53. Lumber yard, Morris Av, Broadway, Division, Prospect. One part.

sheet-40.description: Sheet 40 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and covers a residential and lumber district in the west of Long Branch, from Broadway along the top to Chelsea Avenue along the bottom. The sheet is turned slightly from true north, with a compass rose at the left edge. Slocum Place runs down from Broadway through the left centre and turns east across the sheet to meet 5th Avenue, enclosing the blocks numbered 6 and 7, which are laid out in long narrow lots with frame dwellings on them. 5th Avenue runs down the right of centre and 4th Avenue along the right edge, with more dwellings on the narrow lots between them. At the upper left, at the corner of 7th Avenue and Lippincott Avenue, stands City Hall, with a furniture and repair shop, a wagon shed and a few dwellings near it. 7th Avenue runs diagonally across the left side of the sheet. The tracks of the New York and Long Branch Railroad run diagonally from the upper left to the lower right across the middle, leaving large triangular blocks of open ground on either side. At the lower right is Truax and Cranmer's lumber yard with its sheds, a work house and a pink-coloured building, and below the left blocks a row of new dwelling lots faces Chelsea Avenue. Water pipes of 6 inches are marked in several of the streets, with hydrants and a telephone house. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 49 and 50 above, 39 to the left, 41 to the right and 38 below.
notes: Where Slocum Place meets 5th Avenue the modern junction lay 14 m from the drawn one and was left out of the control.
Chelsea Avenue and 5th Avenue do not meet on the sheet, where the lumber yard stands; the modern junction was left out.
Printed sheet 40, 60 ft, rot +7. Slocum Pl, 5th to 7th Av, Broadway. One part.

sheet-41.description: Sheet 41 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and shows the commercial centre of Long Branch and the residential blocks behind it. Broadway runs along the top of the sheet, lined on its south side by a continuous row of two and three story stores, saloons, cafes, a bank, a printing office, a post office and The Monmouth, whose theatre block carries stage and scenery. The Greene's Hotel stands on the corner of 3rd Avenue and Belmont Avenue. South of Broadway the sheet is cut by Belmont Avenue, Garfield Avenue, Van Dyke Place, Stokes Place and Chelsea Avenue, which run across the page, and by 4th Avenue on the left and 3rd Avenue near the middle, which run down it. A short street named Academy runs between Broadway and Belmont Avenue. The blocks between Belmont and Garfield Avenues are filled with frame dwellings on narrow lots, with stables and sheds behind them. Notable buildings south of Garfield Avenue are the Simpson M. E. Church, the Garfield Avenue Public School, and near the bottom the Lyceum with a parochial school hall beside it. The right part of the sheet, east of the Academy block, is mostly open lots with scattered dwellings. Along 3rd Avenue and elsewhere the sheet marks 6 inch water pipes, hydrants, a fire alarm box and a telephone house. A compass rose and north arrow are at the left edge; the sheet is turned only slightly from true north. Adjoining sheets are numbered 50 above, 40 to the left, 42 to the right and 38 below.
notes: Janes is today Jane Street.
Rockwell Avenue was left out of the control: the modern Broadway and Rockwell Avenue junction fell 12 m from the drawn one.
Memorial Parkway, which now crosses the district between 3rd and 2nd Avenues, is not drawn.
Printed sheet 41, 60 ft, rot +8. Downtown Broadway, Belmont, Garfield, Van Dyke Pl. One part; Rockwell Av left out.

sheet-42.description: Sheet 42 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and covers the eastern part of the Long Branch business district and the neighbourhood behind it, turned slightly from true north. Broadway crosses the top of the sheet and bends into South Broadway at the upper right, where the sheet shows a continuous row of stores, a hotel, a restaurant and saloon, a hose company house and a lumber and tin shop. St. James Episcopal Church stands on the north side of Belmont Avenue near the upper middle. Belmont Avenue, Garfield Avenue, Stokes Place and Chelsea Avenue run across the sheet, and 2nd Avenue runs down the right of centre, with Mill running along the right edge beside the railroad. Blocks between Belmont and Garfield Avenues carry rows of narrow dwelling lots; south of Garfield Avenue the lots are larger and hold a boarding house, the Victoria and a number of detached frame dwellings. In the lower middle of the sheet the Church of Our Lady, Star of the Sea stands on Chelsea Avenue, with a priest's house and the sisters' house nearby. Near the right edge, on the railroad, are Chandler and Maps's planing mill and lumber sheds, with their water supply, hydrants and electric lights listed in a note. The railroad runs diagonally in the lower right corner. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches are marked in the streets, with hydrants and a telephone house. A compass rose is at the lower right. Neighbouring sheets are 50 and 51 above, 41 to the left and 35 and 37 below.
notes: The modern Broadway and Liberty Street junction was left out of the control because it does not fit the drawn junction with the 2nd Avenue junctions (about 9 m).
Memorial Parkway, which now crosses this district, is not drawn.
The part rests on three junctions along 2nd Avenue and is placed as a helmert transformation.
Printed sheet 42, 60 ft, rot +9. Broadway / 2nd Av, Garfield, Stokes Pl. One part; helmert along 2nd Av.

sheet-43.description: Sheet 43 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the left; the street grid runs along the page. It covers a built-up residential strip along Broadway in the western part of Long Branch, from Grand Avenue at the top edge to Oakwood Avenue and the fork of Victoria Avenue at the bottom, with Morford Avenue running down the right margin. Broadway, a wide street, runs down the middle of the sheet. West of it Jackson, Martin, Myrtle and Oakwood come in from the left; Martin makes a turn and runs up the page beyond Broadway, and a strip marked as the right of way of a trolley line runs down the left margin beside Cypress Street. East of Broadway, Grove and Howland run out to Morford Avenue. Most of the blocks are lots of single frame dwellings of two or two and a half stories, with stables and sheds behind them. A few larger buildings stand along Broadway: the Long Branch Hotel at Broadway and Martin, the First Reformed Church on Broadway near Grove, a repository, a blacksmith and painting shop, and the Hand Laundry on the block south of Oakwood Avenue. Water pipes of 6, 8 and 36 inches are marked in Broadway, and a telephone or hydrant dot stands at several corners. The lower left of the sheet and the area between Oakwood Avenue and Victoria Avenue are drawn only as lot lines. A compass rose stands at the top, and the scale bar and the Library map division stamp lie at the bottom.
notes: Printed names Jackson, Grove and Martin carry no suffix; the modern streets are Jackson Street, Grove Street and Martin Street.
Howland Avenue is Howland Place today.
Broadway / Grove Street was detected about 10 m from the fit and left out of the control.
The right-hand street at the sheet edge, read as Oakhill Avenue, is cut off at the sheet edge; the reading is partial.
Printed sheet 43, 60 ft, north to the left (-80). Broadway to Oakwood and Morford Av. One part.

sheet-44.description: Sheet 44 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the top of the page, tilted about 13 degrees from the sheet edges, and covers a residential district west of Broadway in Long Branch. Myrtle Avenue runs down the left side and Grand Avenue down the right, the two joined by Buttonwood Avenue, Art and Kennedy, which cross the sheet from lower left to upper right. The two northern blocks, between Buttonwood and Art and between Art and Kennedy, are built up on their Grand Avenue ends with rows of narrow lots holding single frame dwellings of two stories with small stables and sheds; the left-hand parts of those blocks, along Myrtle Avenue, are large unsubdivided tracts with one or two outbuildings. South of Kennedy, Jackson and Cypress run down the page between rows of numbered lots, mostly vacant or with a house and shed, to a trolley right of way that crosses the bottom of the sheet and continues on sheet 43. A fire alarm box stands near the top right where Grand Avenue meets Buttonwood Avenue, a gasoline storage tank and a garage stand beside Grand Avenue near the bottom, and the right margin carries a water pipe and the Princeton map division stamp. A compass rose with a tilted north needle is drawn at the upper right. Kensington Avenue is lettered along the top left edge and Vernon Street at the right edge.
notes: Printed names Art, Kennedy, Jackson and Cypress carry no suffix; the modern streets are Art Street, Kennedy Street, Jackson Street and Cypress Street.
The modern junction of Cypress Street and Jackson Street (about 40.3011, -74.0053) is not drawn: Cypress and Jackson run parallel on the sheet; it was excluded.
Printed sheet 44, 60 ft, rot +13. Myrtle, Buttonwood, Art, Kennedy, Grand, Jackson, Cypress. One part.

sheet-45.description: Sheet 45 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the upper left; the compass rose stands at the upper left. It covers a residential and lumber-yard district in the west of Long Branch, between Washington Street along the top and Grand Avenue along the bottom, with the Central Railroad of New Jersey running down the left edge. Branchport Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet from left to right. Lane, Margaret, Vernon and Harrison run down the page between the two long streets, and Lafayette, Art Street and Kennedy Street appear at the edges. The blocks hold single frame dwellings of two and two and a half stories on long narrow lots, with scattered stables and outbuildings; much of the area between Lane and Margaret is still open lots. On the left, beside the railroad, stands the lumber and coal yard of Cloughly, Nichol and Company, with long lumber sheds, a hardware shop and office, a wood working shop, a shaving vault with its engine room, coal and lime and cement sheds and stacked lumber, together with a cement block works on the siding. A fire alarm box stands at Washington Street and Lafayette Street at the top, and water pipes of 6 inches are marked in Washington Street, Branchport Avenue and Grand Avenue. A single-sheet label shows sheet 54 beyond the railroad to the left. The Princeton map division stamp covers part of the bottom right corner.
notes: Printed names Washington, Lane, Harrison, Margaret and Vernon carry no suffix; the modern streets are Washington Street, Lane Street, Harrison Street and Vernon Street. Margaret is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Art St and Kennedy St are printed with the abbreviation St, written out here; Buttonwood Avenue is cut off at the sheet edge and read from a partial label (low confidence).
Lane Street / Washington Street was hand-picked: the detector paired the Lane edges with a lot line and put the junction about 15 m off.
Printed sheet 45, 60 ft, rot -70. Washington to Grand, Lane, Margaret, Vernon, Harrison; lumber yard by the railroad. One part.

sheet-46.description: Sheet 46 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left; Broadway runs down the right edge and Washington Street across the top, with Grand Avenue along the bottom. It covers a residential district in the west end of Long Branch and the commercial frontage on the west side of Broadway. Branchport Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet from left to right and meets Broadway. Hampton Avenue runs up the page from Branchport Avenue to Washington, and Russell Avenue and its southern continuation run down from Branchport Avenue to Grand Avenue. Williams crosses Russell Avenue in the lower middle and Dewey Street comes in at the top left. West of Russell Avenue the lots are long and narrow with single frame dwellings and sheds, and several blocks are still open. Along Broadway the buildings are larger: a hall, saloons, a hay and feed store, a bank at the corner of Branchport Avenue and Broadway, a bake house with ovens, a machine shop and a livery or pool building, mostly of two stories with numbered street addresses from 485 to 545 Broadway. Neptune Hose Company stands on Russell Avenue, and a Bethel church is lettered in the upper middle. A fire alarm box stands in Broadway near the foot of the sheet. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are marked in Washington Street, Branchport Avenue, Grand Avenue and Broadway. A compass rose with the south needle shown is drawn at the top.
notes: Printed names Washington and Williams carry no suffix; the modern streets are Washington Street and William Street.
Russell Avenue is Russel Avenue in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Pearl Street is cut off at the right edge of the sheet and meets Broadway on sheet 27.
Printed sheet 46, 60 ft, rot -76. Washington, Hampton, Branchport, Russell, Grand; Broadway frontage. One part.

sheet-47.description: Sheet 47 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north toward the top of the page and covers the area west and south of the bend of Broadway in the west end of Long Branch. Washington runs down the left edge, with Harrison crossing near the top and Hampton Avenue crossing the lower part and curving up toward the right. Dewey and Dudley are drawn as wide diagonal streets running from the upper left to the lower right: Dewey curves in from Washington and meets Dudley, which runs down toward Broadway. The blocks between them are laid out in long narrow lots set at an angle to the sheet, most of them still vacant, with a few frame dwellings along Dudley and in the blocks on its east side. The lower part of the sheet is more built up. Broadway comes in from the lower left and runs to the upper right, lined with two and two and a half story dwellings and stables, and Willow Avenue and Morris Avenue leave it on the south side. Along Hampton Avenue near the left edge there are dwellings, a private stable and a number of sheds and outbuildings. St. Luke's M.E. Church stands at the lower left corner on Washington. A water pipe of 6 inches is marked in Washington and in Morris Avenue. A compass rose stands in the upper right, the scale bar and the Princeton map division stamp lie at the foot, and numerals of neighbouring sheets are printed at the edges.
notes: Printed names Harrison, Dewey, Dudley and Washington carry no suffix; the modern streets are Harrison Street, Dewey Street, Dudley Street and Washington Street.
Dewey Street / Dudley Street was detected about 14 m off the fit and left out of the control; the curve of Dewey Street is drawn differently from the modern line.
Broadway / Dudley Street and Dudley Street / Harrison Street lie near the sheet edge and have somewhat larger residuals.
Printed sheet 47, 60 ft, rot +4. Dewey, Dudley, Hampton, Broadway bend. One part.

sheet-48.description: Sheet 48 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right (about 28 degrees from the top of the page), and covers the district west of Broadway and 7th Avenue in Long Branch. The tracks of the New York and Long Branch Railroad run in a broad band from the upper left to the foot of the sheet; Hampton Avenue crosses them on a trolley trestle drawn as a hatched strip in the lower middle. West of the tracks lie Lafayette and Harrison at the top left and Dudley, with Dewey Street coming in from the left, in the lower left; the lots there are mostly vacant, with scattered dwellings on Dudley. East of the tracks the blocks between Columbus and Wharburton and between Wharburton and Hampton Avenue run out to 7th Avenue on the right edge; they are laid out in numbered lots, most of them empty, with a few frame dwellings and sheds along 7th Avenue, and Wharburton is marked as not opened across its eastern end. The principal works stand at the foot of the sheet beside the tracks: the Edwards Lumber and Coal Company planing mill, with its wood working machinery, lumber storage, glue room, shaving vault, brick engine house and a watchman and no-lights note, and a blacksmith shop to the east. A railroad watchman's house stands beside the tracks near the middle. Broadway enters at the bottom left. A fire alarm box, water pipes and the Princeton map division stamp appear near the foot.
notes: Printed names Lafayette, Harrison, Columbus, Wharburton and Dudley carry no suffix; the modern streets are Lafayette Street, Harrison Street, West Columbus Place, Wharburton Place and Dudley Street.
Columbus Place and Wharburton Place are lettered at the right edge of the sheet beyond 7th Avenue and are partly cut off (medium confidence).

The two junctions of 7th Avenue with West Columbus Place and Wharburton Place were left in the control; a first fit from four points gave residuals of 5 to 6 m there and was corrected once Broadway / Dudley Street was added.
Printed sheet 48, 60 ft, rot +28. Rail corridor, Dudley, 7th Av, Columbus, Wharburton, planing mill. One part.

sheet-49.description: Sheet 49 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the left, as the compass rose at the foot of the sheet shows. It covers a residential district of western Long Branch west of the center of town. Broadway forms the right edge of the drawn area and runs down the sheet; the sheet's top is bounded by 5th Avenue, and 6th Avenue crosses a block below it. Lippincott Avenue enters from Broadway and runs obliquely to the left, with 7th Avenue crossing the lower part of the sheet from lower left to Broadway. Wharburton Place and Columbus Place run diagonally across the lower blocks, and Wharburton Street and Columbus Street leave 7th Avenue to the south. The long, narrow lots are filled with single frame dwellings of two and a half stories, most of them with a small outbuilding at the rear, and the blocks nearest 5th and 6th Avenues are the most closely built. Near Broadway at 6th Avenue a hay and feed store with its adjoining shed stands on a corner lot, and farther down Broadway a larger lot at the Lippincott Avenue corner holds only a few buildings. At the lower left corner a beer depot (Lembeck and Betz) stands beside the railroad tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, which run down the left edge. A trolley line is lettered along the lots beside Broadway. Six and eight inch water pipes are marked in 5th Avenue, 6th Avenue and Lippincott Avenue, with fire hydrants at street corners. The lower right of the sheet is blank apart from the compass rose and the scale bar.
notes: North points to the left of the sheet.
Modern names: 5th Avenue is North 5th Avenue and Columbus Place is East and West Columbus Place (two nodes 13 m apart; only East Columbus Place was used as control).
Broadway is drawn about 60 to 100 feet wide; the modern junctions on it carry residuals up to about 4 m.
Printed sheet 49, 60 ft, north to the left (-83). West of Broadway: 5th to 7th Av, Lippincott, Wharburton Pl, Columbus Pl. One part.

sheet-50.description: Sheet 50 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left. It covers the central business and residential blocks of Long Branch between Liberty Street along the top and 5th Avenue along the bottom, with Broadway running down the right side as the main commercial street. Monmouth Avenue and Union Avenue run down the sheet as the principal cross streets, with Lewis Alley, 2 Alley and Liberty Alley between them, and Rockwell Avenue crosses the lower third. Along the west side of Broadway the lots are narrow and solidly built with brick and frame stores of two and three stories: a department store, a bank, the I.O.O.F. hall, a Masonic hall, drug stores, a hardware store, a plumber, saloons, a photographer's and an undertaker. Behind the Broadway frontage the blocks between Liberty Street and Rockwell Avenue hold closely spaced frame dwellings with stables and sheds, a furniture warehouse and a few shops. Below Rockwell Avenue the lots are larger and sparsely built, with a printing and electric motor shop, a blacksmith and several dwellings, and a trolley right of way and the railroad run along the left edge of the sheet. The compass rose stands in the open ground below Rockwell Avenue. At the right edge, beyond Broadway, the sheet shows only the outline of the neighbouring block along Academy Street and 3rd and 4th Avenues, which belongs to sheet 41. Six and eight inch water pipes are marked in Liberty Street, Rockwell Avenue and Broadway.
notes: North points to the left of the sheet.
Modern name of 5th Avenue is North 5th Avenue.
