The junctions of Broadway with 3rd Avenue and 4th Avenue lie about 14 m and 13 m from where the sheet's other control puts them, so they were left out of the control; the sheet draws them about 300 px (45 m) farther from Liberty Street than the modern ones.
Printed sheet 50, 60 ft, north to the left (-78). Broadway business blocks, Liberty to 5th Av. One part; 3rd and 4th Av at Broadway displaced.

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north roughly up the page, as the compass rose at the upper left shows. It covers the northwestern part of central Long Branch, from the retail blocks of Broadway at the foot of the sheet to the gas works and the Lincoln Place district at the top. Liberty runs down the left side, crossed by Brook, Monmouth Avenue, Union Avenue and Broadway; Long Branch Avenue runs down the right side and meets North Broadway, which crosses the lower right corner with South Broadway beside it, and 2nd Avenue joins Union Avenue and Broadway near the middle of the lower edge. The lower blocks along Broadway are solidly built with shops, the Rhineland Hotel, the Bee Hive store, a bottling works, paint and oil stores and, near 2nd Avenue, the Merchants Hotel. Between Monmouth Avenue and Union Avenue the lots hold frame dwellings and Lewis Alley cuts through the block. At the center the Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the sheet in a curve, with a turntable, a freight depot and the coal yard of C. G. Van Note on its north side. The Consolidated Gas Company of New Jersey occupies the upper middle, with its dynamo and engine rooms, retort and generator houses, tar tank and gas holders, and a new steel-frame boiler house marked as being built. To the east the Monmouth Ice Company's ice houses stand beside Long Branch Avenue. At the upper left, Lincoln Place and Brook are lined with small dwellings, with a public school and the 2nd Baptist Church between them. A sewer pump house, a carriage painting shop and a livery stable stand near North Broadway. The upper right is largely open land.
notes: North points roughly up the sheet; the fit gives about 7 degrees clockwise.
Lincoln Place and 2nd Avenue are not in the OpenStreetMap street data and were not used as control.
Brook is Brook Street in OpenStreetMap, North Broadway runs where the sheet draws N. Broadway, and Liberty is Liberty Street.
Cooper Avenue is drawn dashed at its junction with Long Branch Avenue; that junction was hand-picked.
Printed sheet 51, 60 ft, rot +7. Gas works, Lincoln Pl, Brook, Broadway, Union. One part.

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north roughly up the page, as the compass rose at the right shows. It covers a strip of northern Long Branch between Cooper Avenue at the top and the junction of North and South Broadway at the foot. Long Branch Avenue runs down the left side of the drawn area as a narrow street and ends at North Broadway, where the Arcade Hotel stands at the tip of the wedge-shaped block between North Broadway and South Broadway. That block is solidly built with saloons, a bakery, a beer garden, boarding houses and the lumber sheds and yard of Chandler and Maps, with a blacksmith shop and a garage on the lots just north of North Broadway. The two Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks curve across the sheet from the upper right to the lower right, and a trestle and the coal shed and yard of Kelly and Company lie beside the curve where it crosses Long Branch Avenue on a bridge over the street. The large area enclosed between Long Branch Avenue, Cooper Avenue and the railroad curve is open land with a single dwelling. The right third of the sheet, beyond the railroad, is blank apart from the outlines of neighbouring sheet 53 and a short stretch of Madison Avenue. At the foot, 2nd Avenue and Mill Street leave South Broadway, and a scale of feet is printed in the lower left.
notes: North points roughly up the sheet; the fit gives about 6 degrees clockwise.
The printed scale bar (0 to 150 feet) is about 12 percent longer than 150 feet at the fitted scale of 6.8 pixels per foot, which agrees with the 60 feet to an inch of the neighbouring sheets.
Mill Street, 2nd Avenue and the wedge-shaped block between North and South Broadway are not in the OpenStreetMap street data.
Printed sheet 52, 60 ft, rot +6. N./S. Broadway wedge, Long Branch Av. One part; points carried from 51.

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north roughly up the page and covers the Long Branch oceanfront district between Cooper Avenue at the top and South Broadway at the bottom, from the railroad at the left edge to the beach at the right. Grant Avenue and Ocean Avenue run down the sheet, and North Broadway crosses the middle from lower left to upper right between them and the railroad, cutting the blocks into triangles. Madison Avenue crosses the lower part. The upper blocks are lightly built with detached dwellings and a few boarding houses, among them the Hotel Florence beside Ocean Avenue. Along the foot of the sheet, South Broadway is lined with a solid row of two and three story stores, saloons and hotels, including The Lenox, and a livery stable, and the end of Ocean Avenue meets it near a fire alarm box. Near the lower right corner a large block of buildings marked to be removed stands beside Ocean Avenue, with a vacant building below it. The Board Walk runs down the right side next to Ocean Avenue, drawn with yellow hatching, and a small traction building stands beside it. The shoreline of the Atlantic Ocean, tinted blue, forms the right edge of the sheet. The Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks run down the left edge, with a small building called The Ozone beside them.
notes: North points roughly up the sheet; the placement gives about 5 degrees clockwise.

The drawn Ocean Avenue corresponds to Ocean Avenue North in OpenStreetMap, which curves away from the drawn line near Cooper Avenue; Grant Street continues south of North Broadway in the modern data, but the sheet ends Grant Avenue at North Broadway.
Only two points could be used for the placement, so it is a two-point fit.
Printed sheet 53, 60 ft, rot -5. Oceanfront, Cooper to S. Broadway. One part; 2-point helmert.

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 is drawn at 120 feet to an inch, with north to the left, and covers the western edge of Long Branch around the head of Pleasure Bay and the Branchport creek. Joline Avenue runs down the right side of the sheet, with Hendrickson Avenue, John and Conover Place in the dense block at the upper right, where 7th Avenue crosses the top. Pacific, Atlantic Avenue and River run through the western blocks, crossed by Coleman Avenue and Edwards Avenue, and Spruce and Ludlow are marked not opened. The area is divided into small narrow lots, mostly with single frame dwellings. A tidal creek tinted blue winds across the middle of the sheet, with a boat house and boat landing at its western end, and Branchport lies along the south side, where the Norwood Hotel and its annex stand beside the water. East, Berdon Place and Branchport are lined with houses and shops, and the Branchport hose company and fire department are on the east side. The New York and Long Branch Railroad runs diagonally across the lower right with the Branchport depot and a freight house beside it, and the Central Railroad of New Jersey is at the right edge. Jay, Wardell, McClelland and Washington lie in the lower right blocks, with a public school on McClelland Avenue, a coal yard and a cement block works. Pleasure Bay fills the lower left corner, and the compass rose stands beside the creek.
notes: North points to the left of the sheet.
Spruce and Ludlow are marked 'not opened' on the sheet.
McClelland is Mc Clellan Street, Jay is Jay Street, Berdon Place is Berdan Place, East is East Street and Pacific is Pacific Street in OpenStreetMap.
Modern Joline Avenue and Pacific Street run up to about 10 m from the drawn lines, so their junctions with Branchport, Edwards and Coleman were left out of the control.
Printed sheet 54, 120 ft, north to the left (-80). Branchport: Joline, Hendrickson, Edwards, Pacific, 7th Av, Branchport Av, Jay, Wardell. One part.

sheet-55-1.description: Sheet 55 is drawn at 120 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the left, and covers the Branchport side of North Long Branch west of Central Avenue. Liberty runs across the upper part of the sheet from Vanderveer Place to Central Avenue, with Sea View Avenue and Ellis meeting it from the creek at the top. Below it a regular grid of narrow house lots is laid out along Hamilton Avenue, Joline Avenue, Eastwood Avenue and Halberton, crossed by Rockwell Avenue, 5th Avenue, 6th Avenue, Laurel and Lippincott Avenue, with Hendrickson Avenue and Spruce at the foot of the sheet and Pacific Street in the lower left corner. Most lots are vacant or hold small frame dwellings, and many blocks in the lower left are platted but unbuilt, with dashed lines marking streets not yet opened. The most built-up strip is along Central Avenue and Potter at the right edge, where dense rows of dwellings, two halls and the Trinity A.M.E. Church stand; Brook is lettered at the top right. A bottling house and an ice cream manufactory stand near Laurel and 6th Avenue. A creek crosses the upper left corner. Water pipes are marked in Liberty, Rockwell Avenue and Halberton, with fire alarm boxes at Liberty and Sea View Avenue and at Halberton. A boxed inset in the upper left corner repeats the north side of Ellis from Sea View Avenue to Central Avenue and is a separate part.
notes: Drawn at 120 ft to an inch, unlike most sheets of this atlas (60 ft).

Modern names: Sea View Avenue is Seaview Avenue, Vanderveer Place is Vandeveer Place, Halberton is Halberton Place, Laurel is Laurel Street, Spruce is Spruce Street, Ellis is Ellis Avenue, Liberty is Liberty Street.

Hamilton Avenue / Liberty Street and Rockwell Avenue / Vandeveer Place were detected 15 to 20 m from the fit and left out; the north end of Hamilton Avenue and the west end of Rockwell Avenue may have been realigned.

Printed sheet 55, 120 ft, north to the left. Branchport: Liberty, Hamilton, Joline, Eastwood, Rockwell, 5th, 6th, Laurel, Lippincott, Halberton, Central, Potter. Two parts: 1 main; 2 (unplaced) boxed inset top left repeating the north side of Ellis from Sea View Av to Central Av (cut off by the main map's top edge).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: boxed inset top left: north side of Ellis from Sea View Av to Central Av (repeats ground the main part draws; anchored on one hand-picked point it covered the main part's drawing in the mosaic; needs two or more carried points from sheet-55-1 and a mask limited to the strip north of Ellis).

sheet-56-1.description: Sheet 56 is drawn at 120 feet to an inch and covers the Pleasure Bay shore of North Long Branch around the landing of the Port au Peck drawbridge. The upper left holds the pleasure grounds on the bay: the Steamboat Wharf of the Patten Line built on piles, Prices Hotel, Hotel Avenel, Seltmans Hotel and Pleasure Bay House with their horse sheds, livery and sleeping rooms, and Pleasure Bay Park with a summer theatre, grand stand, dancing pavilion, grotto and a merry-go-round. Port au Peck Road runs from the drawbridge south-east past these hotels to a fork with Florence Avenue, where a road lettered Pleasure Bay leads back west to the bay and Patten Avenue runs north-east through a small district of narrow dwelling lots, with a street marked No Name. Florence Avenue continues south across Atlantic Avenue to Avenel Boulevard through large undivided lots. A creek winds from the bay down the middle of the sheet; west of it stand the Leland Park Hotel and a few dwellings on open ground. The lower left corner shows the head of the Branchport district: Atlantic Avenue, Liberty, Allen Place and Rockwell Avenue with small numbered house lots. The Riverside Hotel stands at the top edge. Most of the sheet is open land, and the buildings outside the hotel strip are mainly frame dwellings and sheds. A boxed inset in the upper left corner, showing the Port au Peck Hotel across the bay, is a separate part.
notes: Drawn at 120 ft to an inch, unlike most sheets of this atlas (60 ft).
The road lettered Pleasure Bay from the Florence Avenue fork to the bay is not a street today; the district west of Florence Avenue has been rebuilt (Smith Street, Werah Place, Winhar Place).

Patten Avenue's south end has moved: the 1907 fork of Patten Avenue, Florence Avenue and the Pleasure Bay road lies about 400 ft north-east of where modern Patten Avenue meets Florence Avenue and Port Au Peck Avenue; Patten Avenue was left out of the control.
The fork of Port au Peck Road and Florence Avenue is hand-picked on the modern Florence Avenue / Port Au Peck Avenue node.
Liberty ends at Atlantic Avenue on this sheet.

Printed sheet 56, 120 ft. Pleasure Bay: Port au Peck Rd from the drawbridge, Pleasure Bay Park, hotels, Florence Av, Patten Av, Atlantic Av, Avenel Blvd, Liberty, Allen Pl, Rockwell Av. Two parts: 1 main; 2 boxed inset top left (Port au Peck Hotel across the bay, no streets) left unplaced.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Port au Peck Hotel across Pleasure Bay (no street junction or modern feature drawn; needs a block or shore corner matched to modern parcels in Oceanport (step 6b)).

sheet-57.description: Sheet 57 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north up and covers the northern edge of Long Branch around Sea View Avenue. Sampson Place crosses the upper part of the sheet and Sea View Avenue runs across the middle, with Cooper Avenue closing the bottom. Long Branch Avenue crosses the sheet on a long diagonal from the upper left to the lower centre, and James Street runs north from Sea View Avenue near the right. Along the right edge the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey run down the sheet beside Fay, with a railroad office building and a long narrow structure east of the tracks. The blocks hold detached frame dwellings of two and a half stories set on deep lots, with stables and outbuildings; the Willow Grove boarding house stands on a large lot between Sampson Place and Sea View Avenue, and an ice house stands in a lot on Sampson Place. A compass rose sits in the open ground at the upper right. Large parts of the sheet are open lots, particularly the lower centre and the lower right, and six inch water pipes are marked in several streets. The south end of the sheet carries a Princeton Map Division stamp across Cooper Avenue. Sampson Place is drawn bending north at its east end and widening as it runs to James Street.
notes: Sea View Avenue is Seaview Avenue today; Sampson Place, James Street, Long Branch Avenue and Cooper Avenue keep their names.
Fitted at about 6.46 px/ft, 3 percent smaller than the 6.66 of other 60 ft sheets of this atlas; the sheet may be drawn slightly small or some modern streets have moved.
The Cooper Avenue junction is a hand-picked point on a street at the foot of the sheet, with only its north edge drawn, so it is approximate.
Printed sheet 57, 60 ft, rot -4. Sampson Pl, Sea View Av, James, Long Branch Av, Cooper Av, Fay. One part; scale 3 percent small.

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and covers the ocean-front blocks at the north end of Long Branch, between Fay on the left and the beach on the right. The sheet is tilted a few degrees so that north points up and to the left of the page. Sea View Avenue crosses the upper part from left to right and ends in a rounded corner at Ocean Avenue, which runs down the right side beside a hatched boardwalk strip and the Atlantic Ocean. Cooper Avenue closes the sheet along the bottom, with Grant Avenue running south from it near the lower centre. Simpson Street enters from the top and meets Sea View Avenue. At the left edge the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey run the full height of the sheet, with a water tank and a watchman's house beside them. The south side of Sea View Avenue is lined with the lots of the Sea View Cottages, small detached frame dwellings, and large lots of cottages stand along Ocean Avenue. The large block in the lower half holds the East End Hotel at the left, a group of stables, carriage and storage buildings in the middle, and the long frame Hotel Brighton with its wings near the beach. Several lots are numbered and most of the large central block is open ground. Six and eight inch water pipes are marked in Sea View Avenue, Cooper Avenue and Ocean Avenue, with fire alarm and hydrant symbols at the left. A compass rose sits in the open area at the upper left.
notes: Fay is Ocean Boulevard today; the sheet is placed on its junctions with Sea View Avenue and Cooper Avenue only (a two-point fit, low confidence).
Sea View Avenue is Seaview Avenue today. Simpson Street is not in the OpenStreetMap extract. Grant Avenue is Grant Street today, but it lies about 20 m from its modern line and was left out.
Ocean Avenue is Ocean Avenue North today; its modern line sits about 15 m west of the drawn one, so its junctions were left out of the control.
Printed sheet 58, 60 ft, rot -4. Sea View Av, Cooper Av, Fay (= Ocean Blvd), Ocean Av, Simpson St, Grant Av. One part; helmert on two hand-picked points on Fay.

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch, turned so that north points to the left, and covers a stretch of the North Long Branch ocean front between the beach at the top and the Central Railroad of New Jersey at the bottom. The Atlantic Ocean and the shore line run across the top of the sheet. Below the beach lie large numbered lots of block 25, mostly empty; a single dwelling stands near the beach at the left and a small building behind it. On the right half are the cottages of the Nate Salsbury Estate: two-and-a-half-story frame dwellings on lots 1 to 8, laid out either side of a dashed Private Drive that crosses the estate diagonally. Simpson runs across the middle of the sheet parallel to the shore, with an 8 inch water pipe; south of it block 26 is nearly empty except for a row of three auto houses belonging to the Nate Salsbury Estate at the right. The tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, several lines wide, cross the lower part of the sheet, and below them block 40 is blank. No cross street is drawn on the sheet.
notes: No street junction on the sheet: placed from one point carried from sheet 60 (a dwelling of the Nate Salsbury Estate drawn on both sheets) with the scale 6.65 px/ft and rotation -94.5 deg (the angle sheet 58 measures; with -86, the value of sheets 61 and 62, Simpson, the railroad and the shore stood about 90 m off sheet 62's lines). Low confidence.
Simpson is not a street today; the Central Railroad of New Jersey line is now Ocean Boulevard.

Printed sheet 59, 60 ft, north to the left. Ocean front, Simpson, C.R.R. of N.J., Nate Salsbury Estate. No street junction: anchored on one point carried from sheet 60 with scale and rotation -94.5 (sheet 58).

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that the Atlantic Ocean lies along the top and north points to the left. It covers the ocean front at the north end of Long Branch, from Ocean Avenue and the boardwalk at the upper right to the Central Railroad of New Jersey yard along the bottom. Sea View Avenue runs down the right side to Fay Street, where a fire alarm box stands. Troutman Avenue runs down the left centre and Simpson runs across the lower half; James Street is lettered at the foot of the sheet. A beach strip carries a row of bath houses near the upper right, beside the large Grand View House with its wings, and the blocks between the beach and Simpson are cut into long lots running back from the shore. Cottages and a large frame house with outbuildings occupy the lots along Sea View Avenue, and the Sea View Cottages are lettered along the street. The left part of the sheet shows the Nate Salsbury Estate, with its lodge, stables and auto houses reached by a private drive, and a cold storage and ice plant stands in the middle of the sheet. Below Simpson the lots hold detached dwellings with small outbuildings. At the bottom the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey fan out into several lines, with a storage building south of them. The compass rose lies over the ocean at the top. Six and eight inch water pipes are marked in the streets.
notes: Fay Street is Ocean Boulevard today and Sea View Avenue is Seaview Avenue; the sheet is placed by one hand-picked point at their junction, with scale and rotation taken from sheet 58 (low confidence).
Troutman Avenue is probably Joline Avenue (Route 36) today and Simpson is not in the OpenStreetMap extract; neither was used as control.
Ocean Avenue lies about 15 m east of the modern Ocean Avenue North and was left out of the control.
The Board Walk is lettered on the hatched strip along the beach.

Rotation set by the lead to -94.5 deg (sheet 58's angle) instead of -86: at -86 the sheet and sheet 59 ran about 90 m off sheet 62 at the far end; at -94.5 the railroad, Simpson and the shore continue across 58, 59 and 62.

Printed sheet 60, 60 ft, north to the left (-94.5, set from sheet 58). Troutman Av, Simpson, Sea View Av, Fay St, James St, Ocean Av, Nate Salsbury Estate. One part; anchored on one hand-picked point.

sheet-61.description: Sheet 61 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that the Atlantic Ocean lies along the top and north points to the left. It covers the north end of Long Branch and the adjoining part of Monmouth Beach, from the ocean beach at the top to Church along the foot of the sheet. Ocean Avenue crosses the upper half in two separate stretches, one running down the left side and one reaching the right edge near Atlantic Avenue, where a city limit line is dashed across the sheet. Fresh Pond Road runs in from the left and meets the wedge of ground at the centre where the Central Railroad of New Jersey tracks cross the sheet on the diagonal, beside Railroad Avenue. A coal and wood yard with a coal dump track on a trestle, a gas engine house and a paints and oils store stand beside the tracks. Below the tracks the sheet shows the closely built blocks of North Long Branch, with Columbia Avenue, White and Atlantic Avenue running down the sheet and Church closing it at the bottom. The blocks hold detached frame dwellings on deep lots, a public school with hot air heat and electric light, and the Asbury M.E. Church with its bell tower, drawn in blue, beside Atlantic Avenue. Near the beach the large lots hold summer cottages and a few larger houses, and the area marked Monmouth Beach is mostly open. Six and eight inch water pipes are marked in most streets, with a twelve inch main beside the tracks. A compass rose lies over the ocean at the upper right.
notes: Railroad Avenue is Neptune Avenue today; the junction with White was used as control.
Fresh Pond Road is not in the OpenStreetMap extract and was not used as control.
The sheet is placed on Church (three junctions), Neptune Avenue and White, and the junction of Atlantic Avenue and Ocean Avenue North.
A city limit line is dashed across the upper blocks.
Printed sheet 61, 60 ft, north to the left (-86). Ocean Av, Fresh Pond Rd, Railroad Av (Neptune Av), Columbia, White, Church, Atlantic Av. One part.

sheet-62.description: Sheet 62 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that the Atlantic Ocean lies along the top and north points to the left. It covers the ocean-front lots of North Long Branch from Atlantic Avenue at the left edge to the unfinished Avenel Boulevard on the right. Ocean Avenue runs across the sheet below the beach with its rounded corner at Avenel Boulevard, and the beach lots lie between it and the water, each with a numbered frontage. The cottages and lawns there include Bowling Brook Cottage and a bulkhead at the shore, and the lots behind Ocean Avenue are large and mostly open, with a few detached dwellings. Across the lower left the tracks of the Central Railroad of New Jersey cross the sheet on a long diagonal from the upper left to the lower right, with a watchman's box beside them. Below the tracks, along Atlantic Avenue, stands a closely built row of small buildings, among them a fire engine house and a bake house, with a pink building at the foot of the row. Hoyt is a short street of 25 feet drawn near the bottom. Simpson Street crosses the right side of the sheet at a slant and meets Avenel Boulevard, which is marked not opened south of it. The right half of the sheet is mostly open ground. The compass rose lies over the ocean at the upper left, and six and twelve inch water pipes are marked in the streets.
notes: The sheet is placed by two hand-picked junctions on Atlantic Avenue only (Ocean Avenue North and Hoyt Street), so rotation and scale rest on one street; low confidence.
Avenel Boulevard is drawn 60 ft wide and its modern junction with Ocean Avenue North lies about 14 m from the drawn one; it was left out of the control.
Simpson Street is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Avenel Boulevard is marked as not opened south of Simpson Street.
Printed sheet 62, 60 ft, north to the left (-85). Ocean Av, Atlantic Av, Hoyt, Avenel Blvd, Simpson St. One part; helmert on two hand-picked points.

sheet-63.description: Sheet 63 is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north up, tilted a few degrees clockwise, and covers a residential district in the north end of Long Branch between Columbia Avenue along the upper part and Atlantic Avenue near the bottom. Church runs down the right edge, where the neighbouring sheet 61 is referred to, and West runs down the middle. North Cookman Avenue and South Cookman Avenue enter from the top near the left, and the title Long Branch is printed at the top. Hennessey, White and Joralemon Avenue cross the sheet from side to side, with Hennessey and White joined by a short diagonal property line near the centre. An alley runs north from Columbia Avenue near the top centre, and a city limit line is lettered across the upper blocks. The blocks hold rows of detached frame dwellings of two or two and a half stories, set on narrow lots with small stables and outbuildings behind, and the numbered lots are marked on the plan. The densest building is along Columbia Avenue and Atlantic Avenue and between West and Church. Between Joralemon Avenue and Atlantic Avenue, and in much of the left centre, the lots are still open. Six inch water pipes run in Columbia Avenue, Atlantic Avenue, West and the Cookman avenues, with fire alarm boxes and hydrants at several corners. A compass rose stands in the open ground at the lower left, where Atlantic Avenue slopes up to the left and the lots behind it run in a fan.
notes: Joralemon Avenue is Jerolman Avenue today.
The junction of Hennessey, West and South Cookman was detected about 6 m from the modern node and rejected; Hennessey may have shifted.
A city limit line is lettered across the blocks near the top of the sheet.
Printed sheet 63, 60 ft, rot +5. Columbia Av, N./S. Cookman, West, Hennessey, White, Church, Joralemon Av (Jerolman Av), Atlantic Av. One part.
